caption: Causal Link
description: A binding from this event to the operation that caused it. Written by the system that recorded this event, which generally did not observe the causing operation and knows only the identifier it was given and the way that identifier reached it. The binding is an unverified assertion by the causing party, faithfully persisted: attribution_method_id records how the recording system learned the identifier, not that the claim behind it is true. Resolving the identifier across a trust boundary generally needs more than the identifier: namespace_uid gives the context it is unique within, and issuer_uid the system that minted it. Where an operation is retried, uid names the call whose request the system acted on, so a retried operation resolves to a single record rather than one per attempt.
name: causal_link

issuer_uid.caption: Issuing System ID
issuer_uid.description: The unique identifier of the system that issued uid, recording which system minted the identifier and would be able to resolve it. This is provenance and does not by itself establish the identifier's uniqueness scope: an issuer may mint locally scoped identifiers in many contexts, so naming the issuer does not say which context a given value belongs to. That is namespace_uid.

namespace_uid.caption: Identifier Namespace
namespace_uid.description: The unique identifier of the context within which uid is unique. Many identifiers worth recording here are scoped rather than global: a distributed tracing span identifier is unique within its trace and not universally, so a span is addressed by the trace identifier together with the span identifier; a request identifier correlated on a connection or a session is unique within that connection or session. Recording the scope is what makes the binding resolvable by a consumer that did not observe the causing operation. Omitted only when uid is globally unique on its own, which is then what the omission asserts.

uid.caption: Causing Operation ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the operation this event is attributed to, as recorded by the system that performed it. The value crosses a trust boundary rather than being generated here; the recording system persists what it was given, without having observed the operation the identifier names.
